title: ArangoDB arm64 scheduling fix on local k3d
description:
## Decision Record: ArangoDB arm64 Scheduling Fix

### Decision

Destroy and recreate the arangodb-single Pulumi local stack when the ArangoDB
operator keeps scheduling pods with amd64 affinity on an arm64 k3d cluster.

### Problem

On macOS Apple Silicon (arm64), kube-arangodb 1.2.42 creates pods with a
required node affinity for amd64, so the pod stays Pending indefinitely.

### Root Cause

The operator caches the member resolved architecture in:
  .status.members.single[0].architecture

If the ArangoDeployment was ever deployed without 'architecture: arm64'
(defaulting to amd64), that value is stored in member status. Adding
'architecture: arm64' to the spec later does NOT update it. The operator
logs 'Scheduling parameters are not updated' and keeps recreating pods
with amd64 affinity.

### Symptoms

- Pod stuck in Pending; describe shows node affinity/selector mismatch
- Pod affinity: amd64, node label: arm64
- Operator logs repeat: 'Scheduling parameters are not updated ... step=CreateMemberPodSchedulingFailurePlan'
- Member status: kubectl get arangodeployment arangodb -n dev -o jsonpath='{.status.members.single[0].architecture}' -> outputs 'amd64'

### Fix (run in order)

    # 1. Destroy — deletes ArangoDeployment, pods, and PVC (data loss OK for local)
    just local-pulumi remove-resource arangodb-single local pulumi/local-passphrase

    # 2. Recreate — operator now initialises fresh member from scratch with arm64
    just local-pulumi create-resource arangodb-single local pulumi/local-passphrase

    # 3. Verify member architecture
    KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster) \
      kubectl get arangodeployment arangodb -n dev \
      -o jsonpath='{.status.members.single[0].architecture}'
    # Must output: arm64

    # 4. Restore databases and dictycr user (PVC was wiped)
    just local-pulumi create-resource create-arangodb-databases local pulumi/local-passphrase

### Why Destroy+Recreate Works

When the operator creates a new member (no cached status), it resolves the
image manifest fresh. arangodb:3.11.6 is a multi-arch image supporting arm64.
With 'architecture: arm64' in the spec from the very first create, the operator
records the member as arm64 and schedules pods with arm64 affinity.

### What Does NOT Work

- Patching pod affinity directly: operator recreates with amd64 immediately
- Patching .status via kubectl: operator overwrites on every reconcile loop
- Pinning image to arm64 digest: operator still resolves member as amd64
- Deleting pod only: operator recreates with same amd64 affinity
close_reason: Reference document only — keep as closed knowledge base entry

title: Restore arangodump databases into ArangoDB
description:
Port-forward to ArangoDB then run arangorestore to load all databases from scratch/arangodump/ into the local k3d instance.

Steps:
1. kubectl port-forward -n dev service/arangodb-single-diejsnkq 8529:8529
2. ROOT_PASS=$(pass show arangodb/local-root | head -n 1)
3. docker run --rm --net=host -v "${PWD}/scratch/arangodump:/dump" arangodb/arangodb:3.11.6 arangorestore --server.endpoint tcp://127.0.0.1:8529 --server.username root --server.password "$ROOT_PASS" --input-directory /dump --all-databases true --create-database true

Databases to restore: _system, annofeature, annotation, cgm_ddb, chado, content, order, stock
Skip: lost+found (filesystem artifact)

Restore _system first to set up ArangoDB system collections.
close_reason: Databases restored via just arangodb restore-local-arangodb. All 8 DBs present: _system, annofeature, annotation, cgm_ddb, chado, content, order, stock.

title: Deploy modware-stock via Pulumi
description:
Create local Pulumi stack and deploy modware-stock to the local k3d cluster.

Setup env:
  PASSPHRASE=$(pass show pulumi/local-passphrase | head -n 1)
  export PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE="$PASSPHRASE"
  export KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster)

Create stack:
  just local-pulumi new-stack modware-stock local pulumi/local-passphrase

Set config (use set-all pattern — one call instead of N):
  pulumi -C modware-stock config set-all --stack local --path \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.namespace=dev' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.appName=stock' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.port=9345' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.logLevel=debug' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.command=start-server' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.image.name=dictybase/modware-stock' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.image.tag=develop-2985bd5' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.name=backend' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.userkey=user' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.passkey=password'

Deploy:
  just local-pulumi create-resource modware-stock local pulumi/local-passphrase

Note: key names use lowercase 'userkey'/'passkey' (differs from modware-annotation which uses capital K).
close_reason: Deployed modware-stock via Pulumi to k3d. Image ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock:92ec242. Fixed arm64 ArangoDB scheduling by destroying and recreating arangodb-single stack so operator initializes member fresh with architecture:arm64.

title: Fix relative path resolution for docker buildx from just_modules
description:
The `docker buildx` command is failing with 'lstat build: no such file or directory'. This means the command is executing from inside `just_modules/` instead of the repository root, so it cannot find the `build/package/Dockerfile`. 
Fix plan:
Add `[no-cd]` to the top of `just_modules/docker.justfile` so that recipes defined in this module execute from the root directory where the main Justfile resides, rather than from the subdirectory.
notes: Resolution: Verified that just modules change the working directory to the module location by default. Applying the [no-cd] attribute to each recipe in just_modules/docker.justfile forces them to run from the root, which fixes the path resolution for the Dockerfile and context. Committed in 7fb71e1.
close_reason: Added [no-cd] attribute to all docker recipes. This ensures that the recipes defined in just_modules/docker.justfile execute in the directory of the parent Justfile (the project root), rather than changing directory into just_modules/ where the Dockerfile cannot be found.

title: Fix just subshell evaluation context in docker module
description: The initial implementation of the docker build recipes used a subshell $(just docker build-args ...) which failed because the subshell lost the execution context of the root Justfile. Fixed by moving the build-arg string construction directly into the recipes.
close_reason: Fixed the path resolution error by removing the redundant subshell evaluation. The build-args are now directly injected as strings into the docker buildx command templates.

title: Add GHCR build and push recipes to cluster-ops for backup image
description:
Plan:
1. Create a new module 'just_modules/docker.justfile'.
2. Define variables for GO_VERSION, ARANGO_VERSION, and RESTIC_VERSION in the justfile, matching the Dockerfile defaults.
3. Pass these variables using --build-arg in the docker buildx commands. This gives the user the ability to override software versions via just parameters.
4. The recipes will be: build-backup-image, push-backup-ghcr, and push-backup-ghcr-multi.
5. Add 'mod docker \'just_modules/docker.justfile\'' to Justfile.
close_reason: Added GHCR build and push recipes to just_modules/docker.justfile. The recipes are parameterized to allow overriding software versions (Go, ArangoDB, Restic) via command line arguments, which are correctly passed as --build-arg to the Dockerfile. Verified with a local build.

title: Refactor backup Dockerfile for multiarch and dagger dependencies
description:
Plan:
1. Define global ARGs for GO_VERSION (1.25), ARANGO_VERSION (3.11.6), and RESTIC_VERSION (0.17.0).
2. Update Go builder stage to use golang:${GO_VERSION}-alpine.
3. Support multiarch builds using Docker buildx TARGETOS and TARGETARCH.
4. Integrate Dagger-inspired container logic in the final stage:
    - Base image: arangodb:${ARANGO_VERSION}.
    - Install dependencies (postgresql14, curl, bzip2, redis) via apk.
    - Dynamically download and install restic v${RESTIC_VERSION} based on TARGETARCH.
5. Eliminate the dependency on dictybase/restic-redis-arangopg.
6. Use upx to compress the final Go binary.
close_reason: Refactored Dockerfile to use Go 1.25, support multi-arch builds (ARM64/AMD64), and integrated Dagger container dependencies (postgres, redis, restic) directly into the image. Verified with a successful local build.

title: Add MinIO local k3d deployment support
description: The minio/ Pulumi module is fully implemented but has no local stack config for k3d. Need to: (1) create minio/Pulumi.local.yaml with k3d-specific config (dictycr-balanced storage, 5Gi, webui disabled), (2) create just_modules/minio.justfile with deploy-local-minio recipe following the same pattern as deploy-local-arangodb, (3) register the new module in Justfile. Credentials read from pass entries: minio/local-user and minio/local-password.
design:
# Plan: Install MinIO in Local k3d Cluster

## Context

The `feat/run-local-k3d` branch is progressively adding local k3d cluster support for
each service. MinIO (`minio/main.go`) is a fully implemented Pulumi module with
dev/experiments configs but **no local k3d stack config**.

Simplified approach: create `minio/Pulumi.local.yaml` with all non-secret config
pre-populated. Credentials are set once via `pulumi config set` (same pattern as other
local stacks — they get encrypted and written back into the yaml). After that, the
existing `just local-pulumi create-resource` workflow handles all future deploys.

No new Justfile module or recipe needed.

## What Needs to Be Done

**One file**: `minio/Pulumi.local.yaml` — pre-populated with all non-secret config.

```yaml
secretsprovider: passphrase
config:
  minio:properties:
    chart:
      name: bitnami/minio
      repository: https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
      version: 14.7.10
    image:
      tag: "2024.8.3"
    namespace: dev
    secret:
      name: minio
      passKey: pass
      userKey: user
    storage:
      class: dictycr-balanced
      size: 15Gi
    webui: false
```

Notes:
- `secret.name: minio` — K8s Secret name
- `secret.userKey: user` / `secret.passKey: pass` — key names inside the K8s Secret
- `secret.userName` and `secret.password` are NOT in the yaml — set via one-time
  `pulumi config set --secret` below (encrypted values get written back to the file)
- `image.tag: "2024.8.3"` — combined with the hardcoded repository in `minio/main.go`
  (`bitnamilegacy/minio`), this resolves to `docker.io/bitnamilegacy/minio:2024.8.3`.
  The `ImageConfig` struct only exposes `Tag`; registry and repository are fixed in code.
- `storage.class: dictycr-balanced` — matches `storage_class/Pulumi.local.yaml`
- `storage.size: 15Gi` — local dev allocation
- `apiIngress` omitted — `APIIngress.Enabled` defaults to `false`; no ingress controller in k3d

## Critical Files

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `minio/Pulumi.local.yaml` | CREATE — local k3d stack config (non-secret values) |

No changes to `Justfile` or new `.justfile` modules.

## One-Time Setup Commands

Run these once to initialise the stack and populate secrets. After this the yaml will
contain encrypted credential values and can be committed.

```bash
# 1. Export k3d kubeconfig
KUBECONFIG_FILE=$(mktemp /tmp/k3d-kubeconfig-XXXXXX.yaml)
k3d kubeconfig get k3d-dev-cluster > "$KUBECONFIG_FILE"
export KUBECONFIG="$KUBECONFIG_FILE"

# 2. Set passphrase
export PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE=$(pass show pulumi/local-passphrase | head -n 1)

# 3. Init stack (idempotent)
just local-pulumi new-stack minio local

# 4. Set all config (plaintext + encrypted secrets)
pulumi -C minio config set-all --stack local --path \
    --plaintext "minio:properties.namespace=dev" \
    --plaintext "minio:properties.chart.name=bitnami/minio" \
    --plaintext "minio:properties.chart.repository=https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami" \
    --plaintext "minio:properties.chart.version=14.7.10" \
    --plaintext "minio:properties.image.tag=2024.8.3" \
    --plaintext "minio:properties.secret.name=minio" \
    --plaintext "minio:properties.secret.userKey=user" \
    --plaintext "minio:properties.secret.passKey=pass" \
    --plaintext "minio:properties.storage.class=dictycr-balanced" \
    --plaintext "minio:properties.storage.size=15Gi" \
    --secret "minio:properties.secret.userName=$(pass show minio/local-user | head -n 1)" \
    --secret "minio:properties.secret.password=$(pass show minio/local-password | head -n 1)"

# 5. Deploy
just local-pulumi create-resource minio local
```

Pass entries needed (create if missing):
- `pulumi/local-passphrase` — already exists from ArangoDB setup
- `minio/local-user` — MinIO root username
- `minio/local-password` — MinIO root password

## Reused Patterns

- `just_modules/local-pulumi.justfile:new-stack` — stack init helper
- `just_modules/local-pulumi.justfile:create-resource` — deploy command
- `storage_class/Pulumi.local.yaml` — confirms `dictycr-balanced` storage class name
- `just_modules/arangodb.justfile:deploy-local-arangodb` — same `config set-all` pattern

## Verification

```bash
# Check pod is running
KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig get k3d-dev-cluster) kubectl get pods -n dev -l app.kubernetes.io/name=minio

# Check PVC is bound
KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig get k3d-dev-cluster) kubectl get pvc -n dev

# Test via port-forward
KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig get k3d-dev-cluster) kubectl port-forward -n dev svc/minio 9000:9000 &
mc alias set local http://localhost:9000 <user> <password>
mc ls local
```
close_reason: Created minio/Pulumi.local.yaml with local k3d stack config (15Gi storage, secret name minio, keys user/pass, bitnamilegacy/minio:2024.8.3 image)

title: Fix restore-local-arangodb illegal database name from lost+found
description: The restore-local-arangodb recipe renamed lost+found to .lost+found.skip inside the dump directory, but ArangoDB still saw it as an invalid database name (dot-prefixed). Fixed by moving lost+found to a temp directory outside the dump dir during restore.
close_reason: Fixed by moving lost+found to a temp dir outside the dump directory instead of renaming in-place. Verified restore of 199 collections across 8 databases.

title: Upgrade ArangoDB operator from 1.2.42 to 1.3.4
description:
Current version: 1.2.42 (arangodb/kube-arangodb:1.2.42)
Target version: 1.3.4 (two below latest 1.4.1)

Installed via Pulumi + Helm release (arangodb-operator/main.go).
Version is controlled by arangodb-operator/Pulumi.local.yaml.

PLAN

Step 1 — Edit arangodb-operator/Pulumi.local.yaml
  Change both version fields from 1.2.42 to 1.3.4:
  - arangodb-operator:chart.version
  - arangodb-operator:properties.chart.version

Step 2 — Run Pulumi update
  export KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster)
  just local-pulumi create-resource arangodb-operator local pulumi/local-passphrase
  (Triggers Helm upgrade in-place; operator pod restarts with new image)

Step 3 — Verify
  KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster) \
    kubectl get deployment -n dev arango-arangodb-operator-29dc600f-operator \
    -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
  Expected: arangodb/kube-arangodb:1.3.4

Release notes: https://github.com/arangodb/kube-arangodb/releases/tag/1.3.4
notes: Verified cluster access method: Use 'export KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster)' to target the local k3d cluster.
close_reason: Upgraded ArangoDB operator to 1.3.4 via Pulumi Helm upgrade
